requirement: Each item's attachments appear in source order.
rationale:
The obligation is that each item's attachments appear in source order. It has one testable property: the attachments for any item are sorted by position in the source. The only implementation site, `Outline::from_legacy` in `contents.rs`, pushes all comments first and then all annotations, and finally sorts them by start offset. So a missing or wrong sort would show up as annotations placed after every comment.

The marked test is `rust_attachments_keep_the_owner_kind_and_original_bytes` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`. It exercises this case with a fixture whose owner item `fn f` has four attachments in this source order: two `///` comments, a `#[inline]` annotation, then a trailing `// trailing` comment. The test asserts the exact ordered list of `(kind, text)` pairs: Comment, Comment, Annotation, Comment. A missing sort would put the annotation last, since annotations are pushed after comments, so that assertion would fail. Mixing kinds in the fixture is what makes the test able to catch that bug. A final assertion checks that the first attachment's span ends no later than the second's start. That covers the two identical `/// café` lines, which text comparison alone could not tell apart. The test also checks per-item separation: the module item has no attachments, and the file-level comment is attached to the first item and not to the later ones.

Only Rust is checked for ordering. The requirement is language-agnostic, but the ordering code is a single shared step in `from_legacy`, so one language exercises it fully. I found no other test that references this requirement, and none is needed.

text: Each item's attachments appear in source order.
